data.title: Brown-Forman Increases Cash Dividend for 43rd Consecutive Year
data.description:
Brown-Forman Corporation (NYSE: BFA, BFB) announced today that its Board of Directors approved an increase of 2% to the quarterly cash dividend from $0.2310 per share to $0.2356 per share on its Class A and Class B Common Stock. As a result, the indicated annual cash dividend will rise from $0.9240 per share to $0.9424 per share. The dividend is payable on January 4, 2027, to stockholders of record of all the issued and outstanding shares as of the close of business on December 7, 2026.

"For 43 consecutive years, Brown-Forman has increased its dividend across changing market conditions,” said Brown-Forman President and Chief Executive Officer Lawson Whiting. “This enduring record reflects the resilience of our business, the strength of our portfolio, and our commitment to delivering long-term value for our shareholders.”

Brown-Forman, a member of the prestigious S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index, has paid regular quarterly cash dividends for 83 years and has increased the cash dividend for 43 consecutive years.

Brown-Forman Corporation is a global leader in the spirits industry, responsibly building exceptional beverage alcohol brands for more than 155 years. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, we are guided by our founding promise, “Nothing Better in the Market.” Our premium portfolio includes the Jack Daniel’s Family of Brands, Woodford Reserve, Old Forester, New Mix, el Jimador, Herradura, The Glendronach, Glenglassaugh, Benriach, Diplomático Rum, Gin Mare, Fords Gin, Chambord, and Slane. With approximately 4,900 employees worldwide, we proudly share our passion for fine-quality spirits in more than 170 countries. Learn more at brown-forman.com and stay connected with us on LinkedIn, Instagram, and X.

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
Key points:
  • Minutes from Fed's October meeting showed expansive talk on financial stability risks
  • Fed officials discussed strategies to manage financial trouble

By Michael S. Derby

Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed.

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored."

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

data.title: ASUS Empowers Businesses with Trusted  AI Solutions at Microsoft Ignite 2026
data.description:
Your IT Solution Partner for the AI Era: ASUS highlights trusted AI solutions and joins Intel to explore zero-trust security at Microsoft Ignite 2026

San Francisco, CA, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --

ASUS at Microsoft Ignite

KEY POINTS

  • Zero Trust for AI: ASUS and Intel will explore endpoint security, real-world device security challenges, and post-quantum readiness in the theater session.
  • Agile solutions: ASUS ExpertBook Ultra and ASUS ExpertBook A7 enable everyday AI productivity; ProArt P16, P14, ProArt GR1X and ExpertCenter Pro ET700I W7 support local AI workflows; ESC8000-E12P scales enterprise AI computing.
  • Always-on reliability: ASUS ExpertBook A7 and ASUS ExpertBook B5 Flip G2 demonstrate durable design, while ASUS ExpertGuardian and Microsoft security help protect business endpoints.
  • All-round partnership: ASUS lifecycle services and Microsoft management technologies, including Windows Autopilot and Microsoft Intune, help simplify deployment, management, and device retirement.

ASUS makes its debut at Microsoft Ignite 2026, highlighting its commitment to helping business customers adopt AI with confidence through secure, reliable, and scalable IT solutions. Under the theme Your IT Solution Partner for the AI Era, ASUS brings together industry perspectives and practical innovations across three core pillars — agile solutions, always-on reliability, and all-round partnership.

Trust That Travels: Zero Trust for AI Starts on the Endpoint

At Microsoft Ignite 2026, ASUS and Intel® will explore the importance of endpoint trust as AI agents take on business tasks and gain access to enterprise data during the theater session on November 18, 2026, at 1:40 PM PST.

Key takeaways:

• Endpoint trust for AI: How cloud policies, hardware security, and firmware protection work together to help businesses deploy AI agents with confidence.

• Real-world security challenges: A layered security approach helps businesses strengthen endpoint protection and resilience against risks involving compromised, tampered, and lost or reassigned devices.

• Post-quantum readiness: Preparing for evolving cryptographic standards and long-term device security needs helps businesses make informed IT planning and procurement decisions.

Beyond the theater session, ASUS will showcase a comprehensive portfolio of AI-powered solutions and services designed to meet evolving business needs at ASUS Booth #451.

Agile Solutions

Intelligent Productivity for Modern Workstyles

Leading the workspace AI showcase, ASUS ExpertBook Ultra combines powerful on-device AI performance with exceptional portability, starting at just 2.43lbs. Powered by up to an Intel Core™ Ultra X9 Series 3 processor with up to 50 TOPS of NPU performance, ExpertBook Ultra is designed to handle demanding AI workloads. Alongside the flagship model, ASUS ExpertBook A7 supports everyday business productivity and collaboration across diverse workstyles.

Bringing Advanced AI Workflows to Local Computing

Powered by NVIDIA® RTX™ Spark, the ASUS ProArt P16 and P14 enable on-device LLM execution for greater data privacy, reduced reliance on cloud AI services and token-based billing and enhanced local agentic AI workflows.

The compact ASUS ProArt GR1X Mini PC provides always-on local AI capacity for agents, model serving, and creative automation, supported by advanced cooling and high-speed connectivity.

The powerful ASUS ExpertCenter Pro ET700I W7 workstation system supports Intel Xeon® W-series processors and up to two NVIDIA RTX professional GPUs for AI development, data analysis, and 3D rendering.

Agentic AI showcase (from left to right): ASUS ExpertCenter Pro ET700I W7, ASUS ProArt P16, and ASUS ProArt P14

Scaling AI for Enterprise Demands

Extending AI capabilities from local computing to enterprise-scale workloads, ASUS ESC8000-E12P is a high-density 4U GPU server powered by dual Intel Xeon 6 processors. Supporting up to eight dual-slot GPUs and optional NVIDIA NVLink® Bridge configurations, the server features NVIDIA MGX™ modular architecture for flexible deployment and scalable performance across demanding enterprise AI applications.

Always-on Reliability: Durable and Secure by Design

Across the ExpertBook and ExpertCenter lineup, military-grade durability testing reinforces reliability for everyday business use. ASUS ExpertBook A7 features a CNC-milled all-metal unibody chassis engineered for structural rigidity and resistance to everyday wear. ASUS ExpertBook B5 Flip G2 offers a versatile 360°-convertible hinge design.

Beyond physical durability, ASUS ExpertGuardian provides hardware- and firmware-level protection, complemented by Microsoft security. Selected models, including ASUS ExpertBook Ultra, ASUS ExpertCenter B900 Series, and ASUS ExpertBook B5 G2, also offer Intel vPro® capabilities to strengthen endpoint security and remote manageability.

ASUS ExpertGuardian, with ASUS ExpertBook B5 Flip G2, ASUS BE27ACGN, and ASUS ExpertCenter B900

All-round Partnership: End-to-End IT Lifecycle Support

Working closely with customers, ASUS goes beyond hardware to support every stage of the enterprise IT lifecycle, maximizing device value while adapting to evolving business needs. Attendees can explore ASUS AI-powered devices, ExpertGuardian security capabilities, and integrated IT management solutions at ASUS Booth #451, connecting the session’s insights with practical business solutions.

AVAILABILITY & PRICING

The ASUS ProArt GR1X Mini PC is now available in the United States starting Nov 18. For availability and pricing information on other ASUS products, please contact your local ASUS representative for further information.

ASUS is an innovative technology leader delivering the world’s most comprehensive AI solutions across Infrastructure, Physical AI, AI PC/Devices, and Engineering the AI Advantage. Guided by its “Ubiquitous AI. Incredible Possibilities.” strategy, ASUS is bringing enterprise-to-edge AI to life. The ASUS portfolio also includes the ROG and ProArt sub-brands, which serve gamers and creators worldwide.
